title: Probabilistic, Edge-Enabled Structural Health Monitoring for Bridges Under Operational and Environmental Variability
content: Structural health monitoring (SHM) systems deployed on bridges must operate under noisy measurements, missing data, and pronounced environmental and operational variability. Threshold-based alerting often cannot distinguish structural change from benign fluctuations driven by temperature and traffic, producing false alarms that erode operator trust. This paper presents Custodian, an open-source, modular Julia platform implementing a probabilistic SHM workflow: continuous Bayesian updating of damage-state beliefs through Hidden Markov Models, classical fatigue and crack-growth analysis, remaining useful life prediction via stochastic degradation processes and survival models, and uncertainty quantification through Metropolis-Hastings Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC), Latin Hypercube Monte Carlo propagation, and Sobol sensitivity indices. The platform integrates quality-aware sensor ingestion, versioned multi-backend time-series storage, and interface specifications for a low-latency edge runtime. Each probabilistic component is verified against an established open-source reference dataset or an analytically tractable test problem. Across eight benchmark suites, the platform recovers the published Virkler crack-growth parameters to within 5%, Basquin S-N coefficients to within 1.5%, and analytical Sobol indices to within 0.015, with MCMC convergence diagnostics (\( \hat{R} \) = 1.001) confirming reliable posterior sampling. A fully specified field evaluation protocol then defines how the platform is to be assessed on an operational bridge against threshold-based baselines. The modular, open-source design provides a transparent, extensible foundation for probability-first infrastructure monitoring research and practice.
